title: 速度敏捷评估
requirements: Accepted sources have a real alpha channel and were visually checked on a neutral background.
Each scene uses one Bojji and one Despa with no readable text, floor, room, cast shadow, duplicate pose or sequence framing.
Overview art is independently generated and compositionally distinct from its corresponding knowledge image.
Speed and agility assessment distinguishes tasks and repeatable conditions without race scores, path arrows or diagnostic claims.

accepted.review: A low deceleration stance and three isolated cones introduce assessment without a race or score.
Straight running preparation and a low braking posture distinguish linear, change-of-direction and reactive demands.
Blank cue card and compact cone cluster show task-led test selection without creating a race route.
Featureless timing token, secured boot and three matching cones communicate repeatable conditions without readable timing equipment.
On-site observation of a low deceleration posture supplies action-quality context without a camera, tripod or tracking markers.
One cone, a controlled stop position and separate slack resistance loop connect results to one focused next step.
Independent compact braking composition uses a different scale and stance hierarchy from the knowledge illustration.
Card and cone hierarchy is independent from the wide selection scene and remains free of route markings.
Featureless oval timing token and matching cones preserve the standard-condition idea without a stopwatch face or button.
In-person observation scene is independent of the wide version and contains no camera or tripod.
Separate slack loop and a low-speed stop position show a measured next training focus.

rejected.reason: The timing prop included a stopwatch-style top button despite the blank, no-button constraint.
The camera prop included a prohibited tripod.
The revised camera still showed a lens, so the valid on-site observation alternative was used.
The timing prop included a stopwatch-style top button and the cones were not visually standardized.
The compact observation scene included a prohibited tripod camera.
